description: AdamW for the retrain (design section 2): --optimizer adamw already builds tf.keras.optimizers.experimental.AdamW in runtime/optimizers.py::make_optimizer with the gamma/beta/bias exclusion and AMP LossScaleOptimizer wrapping; this FEAT adds the decision record (docstring, constant), --weight-decay validation/help, main.py startup line + NOTE + config.json `optimizer` record + resume guard/event, and tests 11.1 a-f. Default optimizer stays adam; no math change. Independent of FEAT-002..004.
steps: runtime/optimizers.py: extend the module/make_optimizer docstring: `adam` ignores weight_decay (so every m4-m9 Adam run had zero weight decay), `adamw` = Keras 2.10 experimental AdamW: decoupled decay w <- w - lr_t * wd * w before the unchanged Adam update, lr_t = the optimizer's current (scheduled) learning_rate, excluded names gamma/beta/bias (BN/LayerNorm affine + every bias). Add module constant WEIGHT_DECAY_OPTIMIZERS = ("sgdw", "adamw"). No change to make_optimizer's math.

runtime/args.py (optimizer group, ~l.203): help of --weight-decay = 'used by sgdw and adamw only; adam ignores it'; in parse_args add `if not (math.isfinite(args.weight_decay) and args.weight_decay >= 0): parser.error(...)`. Default 3e-5 unchanged.

main.py: after the Trainer is built (optimizer slots exist via O.build_optimizer in Trainer.__init__), compute k = number of model.trainable_variables with O.uses_weight_decay(optimizer, v) True and n = total. Unless --quiet print `optimizer adamw | lr <lr> | weight decay <wd> (decoupled, lr-scaled; excluded gamma/beta/bias: <k> of <n> variables)` for adamw (analogous line for sgdw); for --optimizer adam with --weight-decay != 0 print `NOTE: --weight-decay is ignored by --optimizer adam` (also when --quiet is false only; keep it a single line). Add config_extra['optimizer'] = {'name', 'lr', 'weight_decay', 'decayed_variables': k, 'excluded_variables': n - k} ONLY when args.optimizer in O.WEIGHT_DECAY_OPTIMIZERS (default adam runs write the same config.json as today).

main.py: new resume guard `_check_optimizer(config_path, args, logger=None)` modelled on `_check_intensity_aug_device` (l.581) and called next to it in the resume branch (l.367): saved args.optimizer (missing key -> 'adam') != args.optimizer -> SystemExit('main.py: --optimizer X differs from the run's saved Y in <path>; resume with the saved optimizer or start a new --run-name'). If only lr or weight_decay differ, return {'old': {...}, 'new': {...}} so the caller logs event {'event': 'optimizer_hparam_changed_on_resume', 'old', 'new'} via logger.log_event after log_params; the config.json optimizer record is always rebuilt from the current flags (never carried verbatim).

tests/test_runtime_optim.py: add 11.1 a (AdamW wd 0 vs Adam, identical vars, 5 random-gradient steps with changing lr via O.set_learning_rate -> variables and m/v slots max |diff| 0), b (GroupRegLevelModel(4, narrow_config()) -> uses_weight_decay False exactly for variables whose name leaf contains gamma/beta/bias, True for every kernel; exclude_wd=False decays all), c (lr 0.1, wd 0.01, zero gradients one step -> decayed vars == (1 - 1e-3) * before rtol 1e-6, excluded unchanged), d (amp=True -> LossScaleOptimizer with inner AdamW; finite step decays; inf gradient step via the LSO changes no variable), e (checkpoint round trip with tf.train.Checkpoint/RunCheckpoint: 3 steps, save, restore into a fresh model+optimizer, 2 more steps == uninterrupted 5 steps, max |diff| 0). Use the helpers already in that module / tests/runtime_helpers.py.

tests/test_main.py: 11.1 f using its existing synthetic-overfit main() invocation pattern (tiny widths, --overfit-one-group --overfit-synthetic, few steps): `--optimizer adam --weight-decay 1e-4` prints the NOTE; adamw run writes config.json optimizer record with decayed+excluded == n; adam run has no 'optimizer' key; a resume with --optimizer changed raises SystemExit; a resume with changed --lr writes the optimizer_hparam_changed_on_resume event and refreshes the record.

Wording fix carried from design review v1.3 NIT 7 (for docs/comments you write): non-finite steps are skipped by the Trainer's own tf.cond(finite, apply, skip) around apply_gradients (runtime/run.py ~742-755); the LSO's check is a second guard used when it is called directly (test d).
